issues.display_title: Issue #4072: Handle Issue Infinite "Processing Images" Modal on Upload (Images Save to DB Successfully)
issues.main_description_html:
Description

A bug was reported where uploading a panoramic image to a specific tour results in an infinite loading modal (displaying "Przetwarzanie obrazów" / "Processing images").

The issue is a state-resolution mismatch: the upload process actually succeeds on the backend. The image is written to the database and becomes visible on the frontend if the user forcefully stops the process and manually reloads the page. However, the frontend modal fails to catch the success response/callback, causing it to spin indefinitely.

Specific Test Environment Data

  • Target Tour Moderation ID: 3371492
  • Test Level: A level named "tes" has been created specifically for debugging this upload issue.
  • Note: The reporter mentioned this issue seems isolated to this specific tour.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Uploading a pano to the specified tour (moderation_id=3371492, level "tes") successfully completes the process.
  2. The "Processing images" modal automatically closes upon successful database write.
  3. The newly uploaded image immediately appears in the UI without requiring a manual page refresh.

Test Scenario (for Tester / QA)

Preconditions

  • Logged in to an account with access to tour moderation_id=3371492.
  • Tour 3371492 is open and the level "tes" exists.
  • Have at least one valid 360° panoramic image ready to upload.

Scenario 1 — Happy path (the bug being fixed)

  1. Open tour moderation_id=3371492.
  2. Select level "tes".
  3. Upload a panoramic image.
  4. Observe the "Processing images" / "Przetwarzanie obrazów" modal appear.
  5. ✅ Expected: The modal closes automatically once the upload/DB write completes (no manual stop needed).
  6. ✅ Expected: The uploaded image appears in the UI immediately — without refreshing the page.
  7. ❌ Bug (before fix): Modal spins indefinitely; image only shows after force-stop + manual page reload.

Scenario 2 — Verify DB persistence

  1. After Scenario 1 completes, reload the page manually.
  2. ✅ Expected: The image is still present (confirming it was correctly written to the DB and the UI state matched the backend, not a duplicate or a phantom entry).

Scenario 3 — Regression check (other tours/levels)

  1. Repeat the upload flow on a different tour and a different level.
  2. ✅ Expected: Upload still works correctly and the modal closes as normal — the fix did not break the general upload flow.

Scenario 4 — Multiple / sequential uploads

  1. On tour 3371492, level "tes", upload several panoramas (one after another or in batch).
  2. ✅ Expected: Each upload resolves correctly, the modal closes for each, and all images appear without refresh.

Negative / edge checks

  • Upload an invalid file (non-panorama / corrupt): ✅ modal should close with a clear error, not hang.
  • Slow network: ✅ modal stays until completion, then closes — it must not get permanently stuck waiting for the callback.

Pass criteria: All scenarios above behave as the ✅ Expected results, and none reproduce the infinite-modal behavior.

Reference: docs/superpowers/specs/analyze-all.md — see §2.2 (Upload panoramas workflow) and §4 (Tour creation & upload).

issues.display_title: Issue #4068: Implement Set Location Before Apply Request Featured as Photographer
issues.main_description_html:
Context

GoThru has a local discovery map on its marketing page where clients can search for photographers in their area. When a photographer applies to join GoThru, their location is what places them on that map — without it, clients can't find them.

Currently, the apply screen only collects basic information (name, email, and profile photo) and does not ask for a location at all. The GoThru backend has since been updated to require a location as part of every new application. This means any application submitted today without a location will fail silently — the photographer thinks they applied, but nothing actually goes through.

To fix this, the apply screen needs a location step that lets photographers set where they are based before they submit. The step should be simple and familiar, matching what already exists on the Photographer Location settings page.

Goal

Add a location input to the apply screen so photographers can set their service area — either by searching for a place by name or by typing in coordinates — before they submit their application. Once a location is confirmed, it appears on GoThru's discovery map and makes the photographer visible to nearby clients from day one.

Acceptance Criteria

  • A "Set your location" section appears between the description and the Apply button, with two options: Find location (search by name) and Lat/Lng (enter coordinates manually).
  • Entering invalid coordinates (out-of-range numbers, letters, or 0, 0) shows a clear error and does not save the location.
  • Entering empty location shows a clear error and does not save the location

issues.display_title: Issue #4079: Fix Issue Map Tiles Failing to Load (Blank White Screen) in GoThru & 360 Directory
issues.main_description_html:
Description

A critical UI bug has been reported affecting the map components across two different platforms:

  1. GoThru App: Tour Details section.
  2. 360 Photographers Directory: Review Photographer modal (Location tab).

In both instances, the map container initializes and the UI controls (+/- zoom, pin/marker) render correctly. However, the actual map tiles fail to load, leaving a completely blank white canvas.

Important Clue: The map is working perfectly in the "Moderator" environment. This strongly indicates that the map component itself is likely fine, but there is an API Key restriction, an expired token, or a CORS / Domain Whitelisting issue preventing the tiles from being served to the client-facing domains.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Map tiles render correctly with full geographical details in the GoThru Tour Details section.
  2. Map tiles render correctly in the 360 Directory → Review Photographer modal (Location tab).
  3. No 403 or CORS errors related to the map provider appear in the browser console.

Test Scenario (for Tester / QA)

Preconditions

  • Open the browser DevTools → Console and Network tabs before testing (to catch tile requests and errors).
  • Have access to a tour with location data (GoThru) and a photographer profile with a set location (360 Directory).
  • Test on the client-facing production domain(s) — not the Moderator environment.

Scenario 1 — GoThru Tour Details map (the bug)

  1. Open the GoThru app and go to a tour's Tour Details section.
  2. ✅ Expected: The map renders actual map tiles (streets/geography), not a blank white canvas.
  3. ✅ Expected: Zoom controls (+/-) and the pin/marker appear and sit on top of a visible map.

Scenario 2 — 360 Directory Review Photographer map

  1. Open the 360 Photographers Directory → open a photographer's Review Photographer modal → Location tab.
  2. ✅ Expected: Map tiles load with full geographical detail; the marker sits on a visible map (no blank canvas).

Scenario 3 — Console / Network: no auth or CORS errors

  1. While loading both maps above, watch the Console and Network tabs.
  2. ✅ Expected: No 403 Forbidden, no CORS/domain-whitelist errors, and no expired-token/API-key errors related to the map tile provider.
  3. ✅ Expected: Map tile requests return 200 OK.

Scenario 4 — Interaction after load

  1. On both maps, pan and zoom in/out.
  2. ✅ Expected: New tiles continue to load correctly while panning/zooming (no blank tiles appearing at new zoom levels or regions).

Scenario 5 — Cross-domain / regression check

  1. Confirm the map still works in the Moderator environment (baseline that already worked).
  2. Verify the fix on each client-facing domain affected (e.g. GoThru app domain and the 360 Directory domain).
  3. ✅ Expected: Maps render on all target domains — confirming the API key/token/CORS whitelist now covers them.

Scenario 6 — Cache/hard-reload sanity

  1. Hard-refresh (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R) and also test in a private/incognito window.
  2. ✅ Expected: Tiles load on a cold cache too (rules out a stale-cache false positive).

Pass criteria: Both maps render real tiles on all client-facing domains, panning/zooming keeps loading tiles, and the console shows no 403/CORS/API-key errors.

issues.display_title: Issue #4069: Implement Photographer Profile Update Confirmation Modal
issues.main_description_html:
Brainstorming FIle: 2026-06-11-photographer-profile-update-confirmation-modal-design.md

Context

GoThru reviews every approved photographer's profile to make sure the information shown to clients is accurate and up to date. Once a photographer is approved, their profile is visible to clients and they can receive bookings.

The problem: right now, when an approved photographer edits and saves any part of their profile — whether it's their personal details, their location, their portfolio, or their equipment — the changes are submitted immediately, but the photographer gets no warning that this will temporarily remove their approved status. The profile goes back into review without the photographer knowing this was going to happen. This can be confusing and may disrupt their ability to be discovered by clients while the review is in progress.

This feature fixes that by showing a clear confirmation popup before anything is saved — so the photographer knows exactly what will happen and can choose to proceed or cancel.

Goal

Show a confirmation popup every time an approved photographer clicks Save on any of their profile pages. The popup must clearly explain that saving will temporarily put their profile back into pending review. The photographer can then choose to go ahead and save, or cancel and keep editing.

Acceptance Criteria

These are the conditions that must be true for this feature to be considered complete. Each one can be verified by opening the app and going through the steps manually — no technical knowledge required.

  1. Popup appears before saving — When an approved photographer clicks the Save button on any of these pages (Profile, Location, Portfolio, or Tools), a popup appears. Nothing is saved yet at this point.

  2. Popup shows the right content — The popup displays:

    • Title: "Profile Update Confirmation"
    • Message: "Modifying an approved profile will temporarily change your status to pending while our team reviews the new details. Please confirm to proceed with saving these updates."
    • Two buttons: "Cancel" (left) and "Save Updates" (right, highlighted as the primary action)

  3. Cancel stops everything — Clicking "Cancel", clicking the X button, or clicking outside the popup closes it without saving anything. The form stays exactly as the photographer left it — no data is lost.

  4. Save Updates submits the changes — Clicking "Save Updates" sends the photographer's changes to the server and closes the popup once the save is successful.

  5. Loading state is handled — While the save is in progress, both buttons are disabled and the "Save Updates" button shows a loading indicator. The photographer cannot close or dismiss the popup while saving is in progress.

  6. Errors keep the popup open — If the save fails for any reason (server error, network issue), the popup stays open. The photographer can try again or click Cancel to go back to the form.

  7. Status updates immediately after save — After a successful save, the photographer's status in the dashboard changes to "Pending" right away, without needing to refresh the page.

  8. Save button disappears after status change — Once the status is Pending, the Save button is no longer visible. It only reappears if the photographer is approved again.

  9. Only approved photographers see this popup — Photographers with Pending or Denied status are not affected. Their Save button behaviour remains unchanged.

  10. Works on all four save actions — The popup appears consistently when saving: Profile details, Main location, Sub-location, Portfolio, and Tools.

  11. Available in all 17 languages — The popup title, message, and button labels are fully translated in all languages the app supports.

Demo by Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #4061: Bug Fix Photographer Main Location Not Saving
issues.main_description_html:
Task Description

Brainstorming File:
2026-06-02-photographer-location-save-fix-design.md

Acceptance Criteria

AC-1: No crash on first visit (no location record)

  • Given a newly submitted user who has never set a main location
  • When the /photographer/location page loads
  • Then executeGetLocation handles a null or missing location field gracefully — no silent TypeError
  • And the form renders in an empty state (no location on map, search field blank)
  • And hasMainLocation is false

AC-2: No crash when location is 0,0

  • Given the API returns { latitude: 0, longitude: 0 } for a user
  • When the page loads
  • Then the zero-location branch resets state (same behavior as AC-1) without crashing

AC-3: Save + backend persistence confirmed — happy path

  • Given the user selects a valid location via Google Places
  • When the user clicks the save button
  • And the PATCH API returns HTTP 200 and the GET re-fetch returns the saved coordinates
  • Then a success toast appears
  • And hasMainLocation becomes true
  • And the map and search field reflect the saved location

AC-4: Save returns 200 but backend did not persist — silent failure detected

  • Given the PATCH API returns HTTP 200 (success toast fires)
  • But the subsequent GET re-fetch returns null or 0,0 (backend did not actually save)
  • Then hasMainLocation is reset to false
  • And the form resets to empty — the user can see the save did not stick

AC-5: Re-fetch runs automatically after save

  • Given a successful save (PATCH 200)
  • Then executeGetLocation is called immediately after the success toast
  • And hasMainLocation is only set to true by the re-fetch result, not by the save handler directly

AC-6: Save API error handled correctly

  • Given the PATCH API returns a non-200 response
  • Then an error toast shows res.data.details or res.data.messages
  • And executeGetLocation is NOT re-called
  • And hasMainLocation remains unchanged

AC-7: Subsequent visit shows saved location

  • Given a user who successfully saved a location (AC-3 confirmed)
  • When they navigate away and return to /photographer/location
  • Then executeGetLocation loads and displays the saved coordinates and address
  • And hasMainLocation is true

AC-8: Sub-location and existing behavior unchanged

  • Then sub-location save, delete, and load behavior is unaffected
  • And the floppy-disk save button position and appearance are unchanged
  • And onSelectLocation (Google Places selection) and onSetLocationByLatLng (lat/lng input) behave exactly as before
